meta.indexingPolicy: ENGLISH ONLY (INDEXED_LOCALES = ['en']). Non-English routes remain published with robots 'noindex, follow' and excluded from sitemap-pages.xml, sitemap-today.xml, and hreflang.
strictGuardrails: No invented search volumes, CPCs, keyword difficulty scores, or ranking promises.
No conversational LLM tutor claims (coach feedback is deterministic feature-based prose derived from local Stockfish 18 / Reckless 0.10 evaluations and win-probability drops).
No engine assistance during human online Game Center matches (online play is strictly two players and one clock; friendly invitations/rematches are unrated).
No claim that an arbitrary custom FEN / position editor ships in the public app.
No claim that all 30 endgame/opening/fair-play topics have individual built-in endgame drills (only the exact 15 drills in data/endgames.json ship in the Endgame mode).
Existing S3 media only; no local media bloat or AI-generated device renders.

primaryCompetitorEvidence.observedStructure: Organizes interactive Stockfish practice into Checkmates (Piece Checkmates I/II, Checkmate Patterns I–IV), Tactical Motifs (The Pin, The Skewer, The Fork, Discovered Attacks, Double Check, Overloaded Pieces, Deflection, Interference, X-Ray, Zwischenzug, Zugzwang), and Basic Endgames (Pawn, Rook, Bishop, Knight, Queen). Separates themed puzzle solving (/training/themes) from structured engine drills (/practice).
primaryCompetitorEvidence.opportunityForBrassPawn: Lichess Practice requires browser/web setup for many users and does not combine per-move win-probability verbal grading, spaced repetition on missed puzzles, 116 quiet positional judgement problems, and Guess the Elo in one offline native iPhone/iPad/Mac app.

primaryCompetitorEvidence.observedStructure: Separates encyclopedic definitions (/terms), video courses (/lessons), timed Puzzle Rush, and bot drills (/practice). High-tier post-game review features and unlimited puzzles sit behind tiered subscriptions ($7–$17+/mo) and require continuous online connectivity and an account.
primaryCompetitorEvidence.opportunityForBrassPawn: Target learners searching for offline chess training, no-account/no-ad practice, win-probability move grading (instead of noisy centipawn blunder labels in already-decided positions), and transparent pricing ($3.99/mo or $39.99 one-time unlock, with unlimited free Play vs AI, Online Game Center, and 900 Watch games).

primaryCompetitorEvidence.observedStructure: Centers on MoveTrainer spaced repetition for paid book-length opening repertoires, tactical pattern collections, and endgame manuals.
primaryCompetitorEvidence.opportunityForBrassPawn: Brass Pawn explicitly does not sell opening memorization trees (stated on /training: 'There is no opening training. Deliberately.'). Instead, Brass Pawn owns the transition out of the opening via 116 engine-screened positional judgement exercises and automatic spaced repetition on missed tactical puzzles (1, 4, and 10+ day intervals).

primaryCompetitorEvidence.observedStructure: Focuses on importing online games from external accounts to generate blunder-check, time-management, and endgame statistics.
primaryCompetitorEvidence.opportunityForBrassPawn: Capture searchers looking for how to review their own games, stop blundering pieces, and judge quiet middlegame positions directly on-device without handing over accounts or cloud analytics.

primaryCompetitorEvidence.observedStructure: Desktop/mobile apps emphasizing offline puzzle packs (CT-ART), adaptive Elo computer play (Shredder), or offline engine mistake review (Lina Chess).
primaryCompetitorEvidence.opportunityForBrassPawn: Brass Pawn differentiates with dual open-source engines compiled locally (Stockfish 18 GPLv3 with strength limiter ~1400–full, plus Reckless 0.10 AGPLv3 at full strength), zero advertising guaranteed by copyleft licensing, and 8 integrated modes.

primaryCompetitorEvidence.observedStructure: Primary technical and regulatory sources for FIDE Laws of Chess (stalemate, threefold repetition, 50-move rule, en passant, castling, touch-move), Stockfish 18 search/evaluation architecture, and Apple Game Center multiplayer.
primaryCompetitorEvidence.opportunityForBrassPawn: Cite these primary sources in articles covering rules, fair play, engine evaluation, and rating math to establish high E-E-A-T trust.

findings: Standing English pages already record early organic impressions for 'pawn trainer' (/training, pos 13), 'rating deviation' (/ratings, pos 29), 'chess practice' & 'practice chess' (/guides/chess-practice, pos 44.5–48), and 'chess motifs' & 'combinative motifs' (/tactics, pos 47–55).

Before INDEXED_LOCALES was restricted to ['en'] on 2026-10-23, the English query 'pawn trainer' was split across /training (pos 13), /cs (pos 43), /bg (pos 90), and /ru (pos 100), confirming that English-only indexing directly eliminates cross-locale self-cannibalization.

The domain has zero long-tail educational coverage for how-to training workflows (how to calculate forcing moves, how to review mistakes, how to convert king-and-pawn endgames, how to stop hanging pieces), which the 100 English guides under /articles/<slug> directly address.

findings.details: Lines 115 and 117 use `JSON.parse(guideIndexTs.split('= ')[1].replace(/;\s*$/, ''))` and `JSON.parse(guideDataTs.split('= ')[1].replace(/;\s*$/, ''))`. Currently `batch-a.json`, `batch-b.json`, and `batch-c.json` have zero occurrences of `= `, so it will parse cleanly today, but if any future edit or exercise string introduces `= `, `.split('= ')[1]` will truncate the JSON string and crash `postbuild.mjs`.

findings.issue: Price mismatch in generated `llms.txt` (`$49.99 once` vs `$39.99`).
findings.details: `tools/postbuild.mjs` line 285 hardcodes `Pro removes the limit at $3.99 a month or $49.99 once.` whereas `src/app/core/site.ts` line 208 (`PRICING.lifetime`) and `src/app/i18n/pages/en.ts` line 61 specify `$39.99`.
findings.recommendation: Read `PRICING.monthly` and `PRICING.lifetime` from `site.ts` (or update line 285 to `$39.99 once`) so `llms.txt` never contradicts `/pricing` and JSON-LD `Offer` schema.

findings.details: As noted in `product-facts.json`, the live App Store version is `1.4`, while `site.ts` line 81 still emits `softwareVersion: '1.3'` in JSON-LD. Additionally, `site.ts` line 31 and line 80 state `iPhone, iPad and Mac` / `macOS 14.0 or later`, whereas `site.ts` line 79 (`platforms`), `home.html` line 304, and `privacy.html` line 60 omit `Mac`.
findings.recommendation: Update `SITE.version` to `'1.4'` and align platform strings to `'iPhone, iPad and Mac'` when touching `site.ts`.

findings.issue: Legacy claim on `/engine` that the app 'makes no network requests at all'.
findings.details: `engine.html` line 158–159 states 'both engines run on your device, and the app makes no network requests at all', which was written before `Today` feed downloads and the v1.3/1.4 online presence/friends service documented in `privacy.html` (Sections 4 and 6). While both engines themselves make zero network requests, the app as a whole does connect for Today, Game Center, StoreKit, and online presence/friends.
findings.recommendation: Clarify in `engine.html` that the engines themselves make no network requests, while online play/presence and Today use the network as described in `/privacy`.

findings.issue: New `/articles` hub is not yet linked from `site-header`, `site-footer`, or core product pages.
findings.details: Currently `/articles` is registered in `app.routes.ts` and `tools/postbuild.mjs` (`sitemap-pages.xml` and `llms.txt`), but neither `site-header.ts` (`english` nav array), `site-header.html` (mobile sheet), nor `site-footer.ts` (`columns`) links to `/articles`.
findings.recommendation: Add `{ path: '/articles', label: 'Guides' }` (or `'Training guides'`) to `site-footer.ts` under the `Chess` column (and optionally `site-header.ts` / `guide.ts` / `training.html` / `motifs.html`) so crawlers and visitors have strong internal link paths into the 100-article hub.

findings.details: (1) In `.academy-board` (`role="img"`), the 64 inner `<span>` square elements contain Unicode chess glyphs and coordinate `<small>` tags without `aria-hidden="true"`, which can cause VoiceOver to read 64 squares after the board's `aria-label`. (2) `.academy-topics button` elements omit `type="button"`. (3) The `@if(!filtered().length)` empty state has no one-tap reset button to clear `query` and `topic`. (4) `.academy-prevnext` in `articles.scss` uses `max-width: 45%` side-by-side even on 320px viewports.
findings.recommendation: Add `aria-hidden="true"` on the inner square `<span>` inside `.academy-board`, add `type="button"` on `.academy-topics` buttons, add a reset button in `@if(!filtered().length)`, and stack `.academy-prevnext` vertically below `36rem`.

findings.issue: Run `add-exercises.cjs` (and optionally extend to `data/positions.json` and `data/endgames.json`) before assembling `guide-data.ts`.
findings.details: `batch-a.json`, `batch-b.json`, and `batch-c.json` currently have `0` attached exercises (`exercise` field not yet populated on the batches). Running `node research/growth-20261024/add-exercises.cjs` will attach verified CC0 tactical FENs, and mapping `data/endgames.json` (15 drills) + `data/positions.json` (116 quiet positions) can populate verified boards for endgame and positional guides too.
findings.recommendation: Run `add-exercises.cjs` prior to writing `guide-data.ts` so the `.academy-board` diagram component renders on matching guides.
